dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can add/verify federated domains and forge SAML tokens for any hybrid user, including Global Administrator, enabling full tenant compromise via federated domain backdoor.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Restrict to trusted break-glass workloads only. Enforce app instance property locks and prefer cloud-only privileged accounts.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Allows modification of privileged role assignments, effectively equivalent to Privileged Role Administrator. Can assign Global Administrator to any principal.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Limit to break-glass workloads. Monitor role assignment events via audit log alerts. Require PIM for any workload with this permission.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can grant any application permission to any service principal, enabling lateral movement into higher-privileged apps and bootstrapping to RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Require justification and PIM activation for workloads with this permission. Monitor appRoleAssignment creation events.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can add credentials to and modify any application or service principal, enabling service principal hijacking for privileged apps.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Enforce app instance property locks. Move to managed identities with scoped permissions. Monitor credential addition events.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify membership of any Microsoft 365 or role-assignable group, enabling indirect elevation to platform roles through group nesting.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Use administrative units and least-privilege scopes. Avoid granting to unattended apps. Restrict role-assignable group management to PRA.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Authorizes writing Intune device configuration and scripts that run as SYSTEM on managed devices, enabling capture of privileged sessions on PAWs.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Require multi-admin approval for Intune changes. Lock down workload identity usage. Segment PAW management from general Intune.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Full read/write access to all user mailboxes. Enables exfiltration of sensitive emails, password reset intercept, and BEC attacks.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Replace with Mail.Read where possible. Scope to specific mailboxes via application access policies. Monitor mailbox access patterns.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify user properties including authentication methods, enabling account takeover by resetting MFA or adding authentication methods.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Scope to specific administrative units. Use Conditional Access to protect privileged users from property modification.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can create, modify, or delete Conditional Access policies, enabling bypass of MFA requirements and location-based restrictions for all users.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Protect with PIM and require approval. Monitor CA policy changes via audit log. Use policy versioning and backup.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify mailbox settings including forwarding rules and inbox rules for all users, enabling silent email exfiltration and BEC persistence.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Scope via application access policies. Monitor mailbox rule creation. Block external forwarding at transport level.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Full read/write access to all SharePoint sites. Enables data exfiltration, malware upload to trusted locations, and document tampering.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Scope to specific sites via Sites.Selected. Monitor bulk file access patterns. Enable DLP policies.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Full read/write to all OneDrive and SharePoint files. Enables data exfiltration at scale and supply chain attacks via document modification.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Replace with Files.ReadWrite.AppFolder or scoped Sites.Selected. Monitor high-volume file operations.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Grants full Exchange Online management as an application, including mailbox access, transport rules, and organization-wide settings.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Limit to dedicated Exchange management apps. Require PIM activation. Monitor Exchange admin audit log.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Broad ability to modify directory objects including users, groups, and devices. Can be chained with other misconfigurations for escalation.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Swap for granular scopes (User.ReadWrite.All, Group.ReadWrite.All). Partition into administrative units.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify group memberships for all groups. If role-assignable groups exist, can indirectly gain role assignments.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Use Group.ReadWrite.All with administrative unit scoping. Restrict role-assignable group membership changes to PRA.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify service principal endpoints, enabling redirection of authentication flows to attacker-controlled infrastructure.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Audit service principal endpoint configurations regularly. Restrict to infrastructure automation accounts.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can create OAuth2 delegated permission grants on behalf of any user, enabling consent phishing at scale without user interaction.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Restrict to governance automation only. Monitor oauth2PermissionGrant creation events. Enforce admin consent workflow.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify tenant-wide organization settings including branding, technical contacts, and partner relationships.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Restrict to tenant configuration automation. Monitor organization setting changes.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify device objects in directory. Enables device impersonation, bypass of device-based Conditional Access policies.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Use Cloud Device Administrator role instead of API permission. Scope to specific device types via filters.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can create, modify, and auto-approve access reviews, enabling persistence of unauthorized access by approving reviews programmatically.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Restrict to governance automation accounts. Monitor access review completion and approval patterns.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can manage PIM settings for groups, including modifying eligibility schedules and activation requirements, weakening JIT controls.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Restrict to PIM governance automation only. Monitor PIM policy changes. Require approval for PIM setting modifications.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify entitlement management access packages and policies, enabling unauthorized resource access provisioning at scale.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Restrict to identity governance automation. Monitor access package creation and assignment events.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can modify PIM role policies including activation duration, approval requirements, and notification settings, weakening JIT guardrails.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Restrict to PIM governance accounts. Monitor role management policy changes. Require approval for policy modifications.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Can read and modify authentication methods (MFA, FIDO2, phone) for all users, enabling account takeover by replacing authentication factors.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Scope via authentication method policies. Require PIM for activation. Monitor authentication method changes for privileged users.

dangerousPermissions.attackPath: Full read/write access to all user calendars. Enables reconnaissance of executive schedules and injection of phishing calendar invites.
dangerousPermissions.recommendation: Scope to specific mailboxes via application access policies. Replace with Calendars.Read where write is unnecessary.
